neighborhoods_visited: Sawtooth National Recreation Area / Stanley Basin
guide_description: Three days in the Sun Valley corridor: the mountain resort village and its ski history, the compact downtown of Ketchum with its Hemingway legacy and river trail system, and a day trip into the Sawtooth National Recreation Area for alpine lakes and volcanic geology. Each day is geographically self-contained.

days.cluster_name: Sun Valley Village and Dollar Mountain
days.cluster_tagline: The resort that invented destination skiing - lodge, ice rink, and mountain views
days.neighborhood_description: The original Sun Valley Resort village, built by Union Pacific Railroad in 1936 as America's first destination ski resort. The compact pedestrian village clusters around the Sun Valley Lodge, the outdoor ice rink, and the base of Dollar Mountain - a self-contained enclave one mile east of Ketchum.

morning.notes: Walk the main corridor to see the framed photographs of guests from the 1930s through 1960s - Hemingway, Gary Cooper, Marilyn Monroe, and virtually every visiting film star of the era. The Duchin Room bar retains its original Austrian-chalet detailing. Ask at the front desk about the self-guided history walk; it is not advertised but the staff will hand you the sheet.

afternoon.notes: One of the oldest continuously operating outdoor resort rinks in the United States, host to Ice Follies performances since the 1930s. Open year-round - skate rentals are available at the rink building on the south side. In summer the rink stays cold with refrigerated ice while surrounding temperatures can exceed 90 degrees Fahrenheit, which is a genuinely strange sensation.

evening.notes: The smaller and gentler of the two Sun Valley ski mountains. In summer the chairlift may run for sightseeing; if it is not operating, the dirt service road on the south side of the base area gives a 20-minute walk to the ridgeline with unobstructed views of the Pioneer Mountains to the southeast and Baldy's north face directly across the valley. Arrive 45 minutes before sunset for the best light on the Sawtooth silhouette to the north.

if_time_permits.notes: Housed inside the Ketchum Community Library, the regional history collection documents the valley's transition from Basque sheep-herding country to silver-mining boomtown to ski resort. The Basque ranching photographs from the early 20th century are the least expected and most historically substantive part of the collection.

days.cluster_tagline: Hemingway's final home - a small Western town with world-class Nordic trails and a riverside memorial
days.neighborhood_description: Ketchum is the actual town adjacent to the Sun Valley resort, with a walkable downtown of restaurants, galleries, and outfitters along Main Street and Sun Valley Road. Trail Creek runs east of town through a cottonwood-lined canyon, connecting the Hemingway Memorial to the Nordic trail network.

morning.notes: A bronze bust of Hemingway set beside Trail Creek, placed here because the writer spent his last years in Ketchum and died here in 1961. The memorial is reached via a short unpaved path from the Trail Creek Road turnoff - park at the small pullout just past the Sun Valley Inn bridge. The inscription is taken from a eulogy Hemingway wrote for a hunting companion, which lends it an unintentional double meaning given the circumstances of his death.

afternoon.notes: Hemingway is buried in the Ketchum Cemetery on the north side of town at the end of a short gravel path from the main entrance on North Main Street. The grave is plain granite - no literary quotes, no elaborate markers. His fourth wife Mary and his son Jack are buried nearby. The cemetery sits against a sagebrush hillside with an unobstructed view of Bald Mountain's south face.

evening.notes: The four-block core of Ketchum has a genuine Western mountain-town density - outfitters, galleries showing regional painters, and restaurants with outdoor patios that fill up by 6pm in summer. The Ketchum Farmers Market runs on Sundays in summer on 4th Street just off Main. For a quick gallery circuit, concentrate on the two blocks of East Avenue between 4th and 2nd Streets where most of the serious art spaces cluster.

if_time_permits.activity_title: Bald Mountain Trail - Lower Warm Springs
if_time_permits.notes: The lower Warm Springs hiking trail starts at the base of the Warm Springs Express chairlift on the mountain's southwest face, accessible from Warm Springs Road a mile west of downtown. The trail gains around 400 feet through sagebrush and aspen in the first mile before the terrain steepens - most day hikers turn around at the first ridge bench for views back over the valley without committing to the full summit.

days.cluster_tagline: Volcanic craters, alpine lakes, and a granite skyline an hour north of the resort
days.neighborhood_focus: Sawtooth National Recreation Area / Stanley Basin
days.neighborhood_description: The Sawtooth National Recreation Area begins roughly 20 miles north of Ketchum along Highway 75 and encompasses over 750,000 acres of central Idaho wilderness. The drive north through the Big Wood River canyon is itself a significant landscape experience before the terrain opens into the Stanley Basin with the Sawtooth Range as a backdrop.

morning.activity_title: Craters of the Moon National Monument
morning.notes: About 90 minutes southeast of Ketchum on Highway 20/26, this is a detour rather than a northbound Sawtooth stop - plan the day accordingly. The seven-mile paved loop road passes cinder cones, lava tubes, and spatter cones from eruptions as recent as 2,000 years ago. Walk into Indian Tunnel lava tube - bring a flashlight; the entrance is a collapsed ceiling opening about 30 feet across and the tube extends 800 feet. The surface is black lava absorbing heat, so start early in summer.

afternoon.notes: The most accessible alpine lake in the Sawtooth NRA, reached by a 5-mile paved road west off Highway 75 south of Stanley. The lake sits at 6,550 feet with the McGown Peak and Heyburn formations rising directly above the south shore. The Redfish Lake Lodge rents kayaks and canoes at the main beach - an hour on the water gives a perspective of the Sawtooth wall that the shoreline trail cannot match. Sockeye salmon historically ran all the way here from the Pacific, 900 miles upstream - a recovery program is ongoing and interpretive signs at the visitor center explain it well.

evening.notes: A town of roughly 100 permanent residents sitting at 6,260 feet in the Stanley Basin, with the full Sawtooth Range as a western backdrop. The main street is three blocks long. Sunset from the bank of the Salmon River just south of downtown - accessible through the pull-off on Highway 75 near the river bridge - puts the entire Sawtooth skyline above the river in alpenglow. Night temperatures in Stanley drop sharply even in July; bring a layer regardless of afternoon conditions.

if_time_permits.activity_title: Sawtooth National Recreation Area Visitor Center
if_time_permits.notes: Located on Highway 75 about 8 miles north of Ketchum, this is the right place to stop before heading into the NRA rather than after. The relief map of the entire recreation area is the most useful orientation tool in the valley and the rangers here give genuinely specific trail condition updates that the resort area staff cannot.
